notes.text: Austria has moved away from variable-rate lending but retains a sizeable short-fixation share: ECB data show loans that are floating or carry an initial rate fixation of up to one year fell from 38% of new house-purchase lending in June 2022 to about 19% on average in 2025, and stood at 21% in August 2026. That share is above the euro area figure of about 17%, so ECB moves still pass to a meaningful part of new borrowers within a year.

notes.text: Binding borrower-based limits introduced by the FMA in 2022, a 90% loan-to-value cap, a 40% debt-service-to-income cap and a 35-year maximum term with a 20% exemption bucket per bank, expired on 1 July 2025. The Financial Market Stability Board kept the same limits as a non-binding supervisory expectation, citing the marked fall in overvaluation and prices, weaker loan demand and better credit quality, which removes a hard legal constraint on credit as demand recovers.

notes.text: Indexation of regulated rents (Richtwert and category rents) was suspended for 2025 by the 4th Rent Inflation Relief Act, and the 5th Act, in force since 1 January 2026, caps their increase at 1% in April 2026 and 2% in April 2027. From 2028 the accompanying Mieten-Wertsicherungsgesetz counts inflation above 3% only by half when rents under the Tenancy Act are indexed, and minimum fixed terms for business landlords rise from three to five years, which limits rent growth on the regulated stock and lowers landlords' real returns when inflation is high.

notes.text: The headline Austrian residential property price index is compiled quarterly by the Oesterreichische Nationalbank with DataScience Service GmbH and the Vienna University of Technology, with separate series for Vienna and the rest of Austria and for single-family houses and new and used condominiums. The OeNB states that it is compiled for statistical purposes, may be revised at any time, and should not be used as a reference value in financial contracts.
